config.title: useTransition

intro.title: useTransition
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular component that uses the `useTransition` hook to animate the visibility of a toggleable element. You will learn how to manage animation states and apply smooth transitions in response to user interactions. The core concepts involve Angular's built-in animation system, state management, and event handling. By the end, you'll understand how to create dynamic, engaging UI animations using Angular's declarative approach.
intro.usecase: The useTransition hook in Angular is essential for creating smooth, professional user interfaces during state changes. Developers use it in e-commerce filters where selecting categories triggers product list updates without jarring jumps, in dashboard panels that expand/collapse with fluid animations, and in multi-step forms where navigation between sections feels seamless. This pattern prevents abrupt UI shifts that frustrate users, making applications feel polished and responsive. Mastering useTransition allows you to build interfaces that meet modern user expectations for fluid interactions in real-world applications.

objectives: Initialize a transition state using the useTransition hook
Configure transition timing and easing functions for smooth animations
Apply transition classes to DOM elements based on state changes
Bind transition state to template elements for dynamic rendering
Control transition sequences for complex component interactions
Integrate useTransition with component lifecycle for coordinated animations
Manipulate transition parameters to customize animation behavior

steps.title: Import Component, signal, computed, and transition from Angular core
steps.instruction: Add the necessary imports from '@angular/core' to your TypeScript file: Component, signal, computed, and transition.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to import multiple symbols from '@angular/core'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing multiple Angular core features
import { Component, OnInit, OnDestroy } from '@angular/core';
steps.seedCode:
import { Component, signal, computed, transition } from '@angular/core';

// Your component will go here
steps.expectedOutcome: The file now has the required imports from Angular core to use signals and transitions.
successCriteria: Component, signal, computed, and transition are imported from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You imported some of the required symbols, but need all four: Component, signal, computed, and transition.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. You need to import Component, signal, computed, and transition from '@angular/core'.

steps.title: Create the main component class with metadata
steps.instruction: Create a component class named TransitionDemo with the @Component decorator that includes a selector and template URL.
steps.hint: Use the class keyword to define the component class and apply the @Component decorator with the required metadata properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component class TransitionDemo is created with proper Angular metadata.
successCriteria: The TransitionDemo class is defined with @Component decorator containing selector and templateUrl properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the component class, but make sure the @Component decorator includes both selector and templateUrl properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component class isn't properly defined. Check that you used the @Component decorator with selector and templateUrl.

steps.title: Initialize a signal for the data state
steps.instruction: Inside the TransitionDemo component class, define a signal property named 'data' and initialize it with an empty array using signal([]).
steps.hint: Add a property declaration in the class body, using the signal function imported earlier.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a reactive signal property 'data' that can hold an array of items, ready to be used with transitions.
successCriteria: The TransitionDemo component class contains a property named 'data' initialized with signal([]).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a property, but make sure it's named 'data' and initialized with signal([]).
steps.feedbackWrong: The component class should have a property 'data' defined with signal([]). Check the syntax and try again.

steps.title: Initialize a signal for the loading state
steps.instruction: Inside the TransitionDemo component, define a boolean signal named 'loading' with an initial value of false.
steps.hint: Use the signal function with a boolean type annotation or let TypeScript infer it from the initial value.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a boolean signal
const isLoading = signal(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a boolean signal to track loading status, initialized to false.
successCriteria: A boolean signal named 'loading' is defined in the TransitionDemo class with an initial value of false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure 'loading' is a boolean signal initialized to false. Check your syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The loading signal wasn't created correctly. Remember to use the signal function with a boolean initial value inside the TransitionDemo class.

steps.title: Wrap the data fetching in a transition
steps.instruction: Inside your fetchData method, wrap the state updates with the transition function to coordinate loading and data changes.
steps.hint: Call transition() and pass a callback function that contains your loading.set(true), simulated fetch, and data.set() logic.
steps.expectedOutcome: The fetchData method will use transition() to ensure loading and data updates happen together during the async operation.
successCriteria: The loading.set(true) and loading.set(false) calls are inside the transition callback
The simulated fetch logic (setTimeout) is inside the transition callback
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure all the state updates (loading.set and any data updates) are inside the transition callback function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The transition function should wrap the entire async operation. Try calling transition() with a callback that contains your loading and data update logic.

steps.title: Create the component template structure
steps.instruction: Create a template file for your component with a container div, a heading, and a button that triggers the fetchData method.
steps.hint: Create a new HTML file named transition-demo.component.html in the same directory as your component. Add a div container with a heading and a button that uses Angular event binding.
steps.analogousExample: Data Loading Demo
steps.expectedOutcome: A template file is created with basic HTML structure including a container, heading, and button that will trigger data fetching.
successCriteria: The template file exists with a div container, an h2 heading with appropriate text, and a button with (click) event binding to fetchData.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the template, but make sure you have all required elements: a container div, a heading, and a button with (click)="fetchData()" event binding.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't contain the required structure. Create transition-demo.component.html with a div container, an h2 heading, and a button that calls fetchData when clicked.

steps.title: Display the data and loading state in the template
steps.instruction: In the component template, add a paragraph that displays the loading state signal value and a button that triggers the fetchData method.
steps.hint: Use Angular's template syntax with parentheses for event binding and interpolation for displaying signal values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will show the current loading state and a button to trigger data fetching.
successCriteria: The template contains a paragraph displaying {{ loading() }} and a button with (click)="fetchData()".
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have both the paragraph with {{ loading() }} and the button with (click)="fetchData()".
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet show the loading state or trigger the fetchData method. Try adding a paragraph and a button with the correct bindings.

steps.title: Add a button and wire it to the fetch handler
steps.instruction: In the component template, add a button element with a click event binding that calls the fetchData method.
steps.hint: Use Angular's event binding syntax: (click)="fetchData()" inside the button tag.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Similar: button with click handler -->
<button (click)="handleClick()">Click me</button>
steps.seedCode:
<!-- In transition-demo.component.html -->
<!-- Add template bindings here -->
<button (click)="fetchData()">Load Data</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Load Data' appears in the UI, and clicking it triggers the fetchData method.
successCriteria: The button element is present with a click event binding to fetchData.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has the correct click event binding to fetchData.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or not properly wired to the fetchData method. Check the event binding syntax.
